extracted.intended_audience: educated London readership / coffeehouse public; readers of The Spectator (early 18th-century genteel audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A short moral/social essay for a daily periodical addressing behaviour, marriage, literary manners, and public decorum aimed at educated urban readers. The text offers prescriptions, illustrative examples, and an observer's checklist for reporting public conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugal love as the highest refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Love be any Refinement, Conjugal Love must be certainly so in a much higher Degree; the passion of love to a mistress... resembles too much the Flame of a Fever; that to a Wife is like the Vital Heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat marriage-based/deep affection as a superior, stabilizing refinement in character and behaviour. In representation or counsel, contrast fleeting, feverish passion (lovers/mistresses) with steady, life-sustaining conjugal affection that cultivates mind and improves behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to wives: simplicity, friendship, tenderness, constancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters written by Men of Goodnature to their Wives... would appear to have the Advantage. Friendship, Tenderness and Constancy, drest in a Simplicity of Expression, recommend themselves by a more native Elegance, than passionate Raptures, extravagant Encomiums, and slavish Adoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing epistles or intimate domestic speech, prefer plain, sincere expression of friendship and steady affection over florid, hyperbolic raptures. Avoid overwrought flattery; value native elegance of simplicity. (Example contrast given: cabinet of Narcissa filled with sickening flattering letters vs wise Benevolus' simple affection.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict domestic happiness as source of public virtue and agreeable company
rubrics_metrics.description: Benevolus... Abroad he is reverenced and esteemed; at home beloved and happy. The Satisfaction he enjoys there, settles into an habitual Complacency, which shines in his Countenance, enlivens his Wit, and seasons his Conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent or evaluate a character's public merits in light of their domestic virtues. A good husband/wife's private felicity should be shown to improve public comportment—countenance, wit, steadiness of friendship and agreeable conversation are signs of genuine conjugal felicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use classical exempla / model letters to illustrate conjugal virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Pliny's letter to Hispulla is presented as an agreeable Family-Piece and model of Conjugal Love drawn with delicacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ classical or historical letters/stories (translations or paraphrases) as illustrative exemplars when arguing for or portraying conjugal affection and domestic virtue. The Pliny example is offered as a model translation to end the discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observer's checklist for public-manners reporting (Spectator deputation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deputy charged to observe persons and things conveyed between the City of London and Westminster during certain hours, to keep strict eye on behaviour in coaches/carts/on foot, and to send speedy advice of offences or noteworthy conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on public manners, record specific, actionable details: whether persons transported 'give way' to business routes; if meditating young men are studying in public; coach-box young gentlemen's behaviour; whether Man and Wife in same coach appear pleased or tired and 'carry the due Mein' between fondness and coldness; whether newly honoured or wealthy persons preserve former countenance; dress cues (e.g., low-heel shoe, leather-garter) to distinguish discreet persons; country gentlemen abandoning former habits (hunting) for fashions; names/chambers of persistently offending individuals for public admonition. The deputation also sanctions escalating from gentle admonition to public chastisement if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public admonition and examples to reform manners
rubrics_metrics.description: If fair means will not prevail, there is then no other Way to reclaim them, but by making use of some wholesome Severities; and I think it is better that a Dozen or two of such good-for-nothing Fellows should be made Examples of...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For social reform of public manners, advocate graduated responses: gentle initial admonition, followed by public exposure or exemplary punishment where persuasion fails. Practical steps include naming offenders, publishing notices, and using the periodical's authority to 'nip in the bud.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Define rules for salutations/gestures to avoid scandal
rubrics_metrics.description: The general Custom of Salutation should Excuse the Favour done me, or you should lay down Rules when such Distinctions are to be given or omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear social rules about when customary salutations (e.g., parting kisses, embraces) are appropriate to prevent misunderstandings and jealousy. Consider context (relation, public/private setting, presence/absence of spouse), and communicate or codify these distinctions to reduce scandal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat libertinism and encourage marriage through civic measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Too great a Number of the young Men of Quality were unmarried... Augustus assembled the equestrian order and gave honours to the married and reproaches to the single; proposals include fining bachelors or otherwise distinguishing them to encourage conformity with civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To address perceived social harms from widespread celibacy and libertinism, gather demographic data (births/marriages/burials), infer unmarried proportions, and consider policy levers (honours to married, fines or public distinctions for bachelors) to incentivize marriage and stable family formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary and theatrical precedence determined by format and genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of a Folio... set themselves above the Author of a Quarto; the Author of a Quarto above the Author of an Octavo... Tragedian always takes place of a Comedian; Tragic and Heroick Poets have disputed precedence; Pamphleteers and daily writers occupy other places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and observe established hierarchies in the Republic of Letters when organizing seats, honours, or social order: rank authors by format/volume (folio > quarto > octavo > duo-decimo > twenty-four), dramatists by genre (tragedy > tragi-comedy > comedy > drolls/burlesque), and printers/booksellers correspondingly. Use these conventions in social arrangement and in rhetoric about literary esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore proper meanings: avoid equating sobriety and good-nature with folly
rubrics_metrics.description: It was determined among those airy Criticks, that the Appellation of a Sober Man should signify a Spiritless Fellow... Good-Nature... came first to be render'd suspicious, and in danger of being transferred... to Folly. I have had an Ambition... to restore... the proper Ideas of things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In criticism and representation, resist fashionable inversions that make sobriety or good-nature appear weak or foolish. Aim to reclaim and portray these qualities in their true, positive senses: sobriety as steadiness and good-nature as a virtue, not as silliness or folly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid literary affectation of amorous persona; prefer sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: We have Lovers in Prose innumerable... All our Pretenders to Rhyme are professed Inamorato's; and there is scarce a Poet, good or bad, to be heard of, who has not some real or supposed Sacharissa to improve his Vein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique or avoid the fashionable, contrived persona of perpetual lover used to inflate poetic authority. In creative writing, prefer genuine feeling (especially grounded in conjugal constancy) over the fashionable affectation of inamorato posturing used to solicit applause.
